items.t: Southern Company stock faces $1.75 billion equity-unit offering
sum: Southern Company priced a new equity-unit offering on Thursday, November 12, as the utility seeks additional funding for debt management and corporate investment. The company disclosed the transaction in a Southern Company release.

The offering comprises 35 million Series A Equity Units with a stated amount of 50 US dollars each, for an aggregate stated amount of 1.75 billion US dollars. Each unit combines a contract to purchase Southern Company common stock in the future with fractional interests in two series of remarketable senior notes.

Annual distributions are set at 8.625 percent. The transaction is expected to close on Tuesday, November 17, subject to customary closing conditions. The company also granted the underwriters an option for up to 5 million additional units to cover over-allotments.

Southern Company expects net proceeds of about 1.724 billion US dollars before other offering expenses, or 1.970 billion US dollars if the over-allotment option is exercised in full. About 135.3 million US dollars is intended for the repurchase of approximately 125.8 million US dollars of convertible notes due in June 2027.

The remaining proceeds are earmarked for short-term debt repayment and general corporate purposes, including investments in subsidiaries. The company serves 9 million customers across the Southeast and beyond through its operating businesses.

The equity units create a new financing obligation and include a future stock-purchase requirement no later than December 15, 2029, subject to the terms disclosed in the offering. Investors will therefore weigh the additional funding against Southern Company's capital needs and its plans for continued energy infrastructure investment.

items.t: Southern Company stock: 2026 earnings outlook rises to $4.70
sum: Southern Company is lifting its earnings outlook as power demand from data centers accelerates. A November 12 report by Quotelinks said the utility raised its full-year 2026 adjusted earnings target to approximately 4.70 US dollars per share after third-quarter adjusted earnings reached 1.94 US dollars per share.

The report said data center electricity use rose 59 percent year over year in the third quarter and 52 percent during the first nine months of 2026. Weather-adjusted commercial electricity sales increased 7.3 percent, while weather-normalized retail sales grew 3.5 percent.

Southern Company had about 21 gigawatts of signed contracts with large-load customers at the end of the third quarter, according to the report. A further 7 gigawatts of potential business remained under advanced negotiation across Mississippi, Alabama and Georgia.

The demand outlook also carries substantial capital requirements. Chief Financial Officer David Poroch outlined roughly 4 billion US dollars of additional infrastructure investment beyond the existing 81 billion US dollar base capital program. The projects include natural gas facilities, pipeline expansion and nuclear upgrades linked to a partnership with Google. The five-year capital budget could approach 100 billion US dollars if further projects receive regulatory approval.

Southern Company expects remaining equity needs of about 2 billion US dollars through 2030 and is targeting a funds-from-operations-to-debt ratio of 17 percent by 2029. For investors, the combination of contracted demand and a large construction program creates a growth opportunity while keeping financing, regulation and execution in focus.

sum: Southern Company Prices $1.75 Billion 2026 Series A Equity Units Offering

Southern Company has priced an offering of 35 million 2026 Series A Equity Units, according to a press release issued by the company. Each unit carries a stated amount of $50, bringing the aggregate stated amount to $1.75 billion, and combines a contract to purchase Southern Company common stock in the future with fractional beneficial ownership interests in two series of remarketable senior notes.

The note components consist of a 1/40 undivided beneficial ownership interest in Series 2026C Remarketable Senior Notes due 2031 with a $1,000 principal amount and a matching 1/40 interest in Series 2026D Remarketable Senior Notes due 2034, also with a $1,000 principal amount. Remarketing of each note series may begin no earlier than June 13, 2029. The offering is expected to close on November 17, 2026, subject to customary closing conditions.

Total annual distributions on the units are set at 8.625 percent, made up of interest on both note series and payments under the stock purchase contracts. The reference price is $92.47 per share, while the threshold appreciation price is $115.58 per share, a premium of roughly 25.0 percent over the reference price. Holders must purchase a variable number of common shares no later than December 15, 2029, or the next business day if that date falls on a non-business day.

Southern Company has granted the underwriters an option to buy up to 5 million additional units, representing an extra $250 million in aggregate stated amount, during the 13-day period starting on and including the initial issuance date. The option is intended solely to cover over-allotments.

Estimated net proceeds are approximately $1.724 billion, or $1.970 billion if the over-allotment option is fully exercised, after underwriting discounts and commissions but before other offering expenses. The company plans to direct about $135.3 million of the net proceeds toward repurchasing roughly $125.8 million in aggregate principal amount of its Series 2024A 4.50% Convertible Senior Notes due June 15, 2027. Those repurchases would occur through individually negotiated transactions with a limited number of holders, effected through one of the underwriters or an affiliate.

Southern Company stock faces renewed pension litigation in Georgia
sum: Southern Company faces a renewed pension dispute after a Georgia federal judge refused on Monday, November 9, 2026, to dismiss a proposed class action brought by company pensioners. The ruling allows claims over allegedly reduced annuity benefits to move toward discovery, according to Cohen Milstein, which summarized the Law360 report.

The proposed class includes former Southern Co. workers who allege that outdated actuarial assumptions were used when single-life annuities were converted into joint-and-survivor benefits. The retirees argue that older mortality tables produced lower payments than updated assumptions would have generated.

U.S. District Judge Steve C. Jones found that the allegations plausibly described a breach of fiduciary duties under the Employee Retirement Income Security Act. The claims also concern Southern Co.'s retirement plan committee, which the plaintiffs say knew that newer assumptions reflected longer life expectancy.

The order does not establish liability or determine damages. The judge also deferred the question of whether ERISA required the fiduciary to depart from pension-plan terms that allegedly conflicted with federal benefits law.

The case now moves toward discovery, leaving the potential financial and administrative consequences unresolved. For investors, the immediate issue is the continuation of the pension dispute rather than a concluded liability.

Southern Company stock gets earnings boost as revenue rises 13%
sum: Southern Company reported stronger third-quarter results on Thursday, November 5, 2026, with adjusted earnings benefiting from warmer weather, higher customer usage and growing demand from large commercial and industrial customers. The company disclosed the figures in a PR Newswire release.

Southern Company reported third-quarter net income of 2.046 billion US dollars, up from 1.711 billion US dollars in the same period of 2025. Reported earnings per share rose to 1.77 US dollars from 1.55 US dollars. Excluding selected items, earnings increased to 2.242 billion US dollars, or 1.94 US dollars per share, from 1.766 billion US dollars, or 1.60 US dollars per share.

Operating revenue rose to 8.843 billion US dollars from 7.823 billion US dollars, an increase of 13.0 percent. The company attributed the improvement in adjusted earnings to warmer weather, increased usage, customer growth, higher revenue from large commercial and industrial customers and stronger earnings at Southern Power.

Those gains were partly offset by higher non-fuel operating expenses, higher taxes other than income taxes and dilution from additional shares outstanding. Southern Company also recorded charges tied to wind-facility repowering, debt extinguishment and estimated losses related to Nicor Gas capital investments.

Traditional electric operating companies remained the main earnings contributor. Their net income available to common shareholders rose to 2.272 billion US dollars from 1.920 billion US dollars. Southern Power reported 52 million US dollars of net income, compared with 3 million US dollars a year earlier, while Southern Company Gas contributed 21 million US dollars, down from 25 million US dollars.

Chief Executive Chris Womack said the Southeast is growing at a pace that is "unprecedented and transformational" and that Southern Company is positioned to serve the increased demand. The release also highlights risks tied to the scale and timing of future electricity demand, new generation and transmission investment, capital access and revenue recovery.
For the first nine months of 2026, operating revenue reached 24.218 billion US dollars, up 7.3 percent from the prior-year period.

Southern Company Approves Rate Cut for Georgia Power Customers
sum: The Southern Company's SO subsidiary, the Georgia Public Service Commission (PSC), has approved a plan that will lower overall electricity rates for Georgia Power customers, delivering meaningful savings to households and businesses across the state. Under the approved framework, a typical residential customer using 1,000 kilowatt-hours of electricity per month will save approximately $50 annually, equivalent to about $4.04 per month.

The decision is expected to generate total annual savings of roughly $285 million for Georgia Power's customer base, providing financial relief as energy consumption typically rises during the summer months.

Georgia PSC's approval follows a stipulated agreement inked between Georgia Power and the Public Interest Advocacy Staff of the Georgia PSC. The agreement addressed two regulatory proceedings filed earlier this year: the Fuel Cost Recovery case and the Storm Cost Recovery case.

These proceedings focused on recovering costs associated with fuel used to operate power generation facilities and expenses incurred while restoring electricity service following severe weather events, including Hurricane Helene in 2024. The approved plan balances cost recovery needs with customer affordability, enabling lower overall rates while maintaining reliable service.
Georgia PSC welcomed the commission's decision, emphasizing its ongoing efforts to operate efficiently and deliver dependable energy at competitive prices.

According to company leadership, the approved rate reduction comes at a critical time, helping customers manage electricity expenses during periods of higher seasonal demand. The decision follows months of regulatory review, public hearings and collaboration between the utility, PSC staff and other stakeholders.

For more than 140 years, Georgia PSC has served customers across the state, focusing on reliability and affordability. The company notes that since 1990, its rates have averaged approximately 15% below the national average.

1 Company Set to Make a Fortune From the $1.7 Trillion Data Center Build-Out
sum: The build-out of data centers, not including IT hardware spending, is expected to cost about $1.7 trillion through the end of the decade, according to a study by McKinsey & Company. Southern Company (SO -1.07%) is uniquely positioned to benefit from that spending, driven by its geographic footprint, recent infrastructure completions, and a supportive regulatory environment.

The energy company serves 9 million customers and businesses through its subsidiaries, delivering electricity to Georgia, Alabama, and Mississippi, and natural gas to Georgia, Illinois, Virginia, and Tennessee.

The stock has significantly underperformed both the S&P 500 and the State Street Utilities Select Sector SPDR ETF in total return over the past year. Here are three reasons why I think the stock is significantly oversold and presents an opportunity for investors.
The Southeast, particularly Georgia, has become a top destination for hyperscalers, such as Alphabet, Meta Platforms, and Microsoft, looking for lower land and energy costs.

Southern Company recently increased its 2026-2030 capital spending plan to $81 billion in anticipation of that demand. The company has already fully contracted 10 gigawatts (GW) for large-load customers, much of it from gas turbines that can be brought online quickly as data centers ramp up, and Southern is anticipating a staggering 75 GW pipeline of potential data center interest.

Commercial electricity sales, which data centers drive, are expected to grow by roughly 20% annually through the end of the decade, according to CFO David P. Poroch, powering Southern's revenue growth.

The company was criticized in 2023 for huge cost overruns and delays for its Vogtle nuclear power plants near Waynesboro, Georgia. However, that spending is about to pay off. Data center operators have aggressive carbon-neutral goals but require steady reliability that solar and wind alone cannot provide without massive storage.

items.t: Southern Company reports fourth-quarter and full-year 2025 earnings
sum: ATLANTA, Feb. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Southern Company today reported fourth-quarter earnings of $416 million, or $0.38 per share, in 2025 compared with earnings of $534 million, or $0.49 per share, in the fourth quarter of 2024. Southern Company also reported full-year 2025 earnings of $4.3 billion, or $3.94 per share, compared with $4.4 billion, or $4.02 per share, in 2024.

Excluding the items described under "Net Income – Excluding Items" in the table below, Southern Company earned $612 million, or $0.55 per share, during the fourth quarter of 2025, compared with $544 million, or $0.50 per share, during the fourth quarter of 2024. For the full-year 2025, excluding these items, Southern Company earned $4.7 billion, or $4.30 per share, compared with $4.4 billion, or $4.05 per share, for 2024.

Adjusted earnings drivers for the full year 2025, as compared with 2024, were higher utility revenues, partially offset by higher non-fuel operations and maintenance expenses, depreciation and amortization, and interest expense.

Fourth-quarter 2025 operating revenues were $7.0 billion, compared with $6.3 billion for the fourth quarter of 2024, an increase of 10.1%. Operating revenues for the full year 2025 were $29.6 billion, compared with $26.7 billion in 2024, an increase of 10.6%.

"2025 was another outstanding year for Southern Company, and it was also a transformative one. Southern Company is meeting the growing demand responsibly, while continuing to deliver value and benefits to all of our customers," said Chris Womack, chairman, president and CEO. "Taking a disciplined, all-of-the-above approach is how we will continue to operate our company to serve this projected generational growth in a way that supports rate stability and helps drive long-term savings for our customers. Our nearly 30,000 employees remain committed to putting customers first, working every day to help keep costs down and provide reliable energy to the communities we are privileged to serve."
Southern Company's fourth-quarter and full-year earnings slides with supplemental financial information, including earnings guidance, are available at investor.southerncompany.com.
